C-SEC-GITLEAKS-CHECKSUM.Summary: Verify the pinned Gitleaks CI archive against a committed SHA-256 digest before any byte of it is extracted or executed, and fail the docs-security job closed on mismatch.
C-SEC-GITLEAKS-CHECKSUM.Problem: The docs-security job in .github/workflows/release-governance.yml downloads gitleaks_8.30.1_linux_x64.tar.gz from the pinned v8.30.1 release URL and pipes it directly into tar, then immediately executes gitleaks version and the security_gate.py scan-diff leak check. Nothing compares the downloaded bytes to an expected checksum or signature between download and first execution, so a substituted archive at the same URL would run attacker-controlled code on the runner and could falsify the pull-request leak-scan verdict. Confirmed by security review finding F-011 ci-executes-unverified-gitleaks-archive and dependencies review finding F-005 gitleaks-download-without-digest at commit be2f52f880bc453891ec623169d12b0162b4bd3d.

Goals.Goal: Replace the curl-to-tar pipe in the docs-security install step with download to a temporary file, a strict SHA-256 check against a committed lowercase 64-hex digest recorded in the same workflow, and extraction of only the gitleaks binary strictly after the check passes; any mismatch exits nonzero before extraction or execution.

Keep the archive version pin and the digest pin together as one reviewed unit: the workflow comment ties the digest to the exact v8.30.1 linux_x64 archive and to the owner's local gate version, so a future bump cannot change the URL without changing the digest in the same change.

Pin the fail-closed ordering in tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js against the checked-in workflow source, including a red control that rejects a workflow where the digest check is missing, non-strict, or ordered after extraction or first execution.

Constraints.Constraint: Only the docs-security "install pinned Gitleaks" step in .github/workflows/release-governance.yml, its source pins in tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js, that file's local GRACE markup (MODULE_CONTRACT/CHANGE_SUMMARY with a version bump), and the M-046 SummaryDelta in .grace/graph/features.xml may change. Job set, triggers, permissions (contents: read), concurrency, checkout parameters and every other step keep their current behavior.

The committed digest must be the SHA-256 of the exact upstream artifact gitleaks_8.30.1_linux_x64.tar.gz from the gitleaks v8.30.1 release, derived from the release's published checksum listing and confirmed out-of-band during this change's review (second independent source, or the owner's locally installed gate archive of the same version); the reviewed diff of this change is the trust anchor for the literal value. The digest is never fetched at runtime from the same release channel it authenticates.

Verification is digest-only and stdlib-only on the runner (sha256sum); no new external action, dependency, or trust-material download is added, and the verification step must not swallow the check's exit status (no piping the check into extraction).
No release, tag, signing, publication, version or scan-rule actions; the local gate in tools/security_gate.py is unchanged.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No cryptographic signature verification (Sigstore, GPG or minisign) for the Gitleaks archive; checksum only, as the findings' minimal fix describes.
No digest or integrity pinning for other downloaded tools or actions (cosign installer, Rust toolchain, npx-resolved test runners), and no change to the npx findings' separate remediation.
No change to the Gitleaks version, scan rules, configs, the docs-security job's purpose, or the release.yml signing environment (that exposure is the separately tracked signing-environment finding).
No new job, workflow file, secret, environment or cache policy.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The docs-security install step downloads the archive to a file, verifies it with sha256sum --check --strict (or an equivalent strict comparison that cannot pass on mismatch) against the committed 64-hex digest, and extracts gitleaks to /usr/local/bin and runs gitleaks version only after a passing check; the curl-piped-into-tar form no longer exists, so verification cannot be bypassed.

A tampered-digest fixture or mutation of the workflow source fails the new tests before any extraction ordering, proving fail-closed behavior: missing digest constant, non-strict check, and check-after-extraction are each rejected with a distinct expectation.

The digest constant and the v8.30.1 URL pin are bound in the same step with a comment requiring them to bump together with the owner's local gate version, and the test asserts both the version string and the 64-hex constant are present in the docs-security job source.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized: release-governance.yml MODULE_CONTRACT SCOPE/DEPENDS still state the truth about the verified install, CHANGE_SUMMARY gains the C-SEC-GITLEAKS-CHECKSUM entry with a patch/minor version bump, and .grace/graph/features.xml gains the M-046 SummaryDelta recording the verified-install boundary.
The focused governance regressions and action-reference checks pass with the new pins; no other workflow, job, trigger, permission, secret or rule changes appear in the diff.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Green focused governance regressions including the new docs-security checksum pins and their red controls; a workflow diff limited to the install step plus GRACE markup; the graph SummaryDelta present; the digest derivation (checksum listing source and out-of-band confirmation) recorded in the change bundle before merge.

Assumptions.Assumption: sha256sum from coreutils is available on ubuntu-latest runners, so verification needs no new tooling.

The concrete digest hex value is filled in at implementation time from the trusted sources named in Constraints; this spec deliberately does not invent the value, and an implementation that cannot show its derivation is not approval-ready.

Upstream serves byte-stable release assets at the pinned v8.30.1 URL for the lifetime of the pin; if the artifact is ever re-published with different bytes, the digest mismatch stops CI as designed and forces a conscious re-pin.
